title: MingCute Screenshot Quality Recovery batch 007
review_goal: Differentiate five MingCute building variants with screenshot grounded depicts and deterministic evidence fields.

items.depicts_observation: Short rectangular building with three stacked windows and a smaller rear block
items.context_bias: Use when the interface needs a simple city building with windows and a short side extension.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for peaked or tower heavy buildings when the main form is a flat topped block.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot shows the clearest flat roof block with three windows and a small second volume.

items.depicts_observation: Tall slanted tower with a smaller rear block on the same ground line
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants a modern building with a strong diagonal roofline.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for flat roof or centered doorway buildings when the tall slanted face is the visible cue.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot stands out by using one tall diagonal tower face beside a shorter rear block.

items.depicts_observation: Tall rectangular building with four round windows and a centered doorway
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants a front facing tall building with a visible entrance door.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for winged or slanted buildings when the centered doorway and four windows matter.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot is the only selected building with a door centered below four windows.

items.depicts_observation: Symmetrical peaked building with two tall side panels on a shared base
items.context_bias: Use when the interface needs a balanced building with a sharp center peak rather than windows.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for tower blocks when the main cue is the peaked roofline and two side faces.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot forms a symmetrical peaked shell instead of a tower or block with visible windows.

items.depicts_observation: Central tower building with side wings and three stacked windows
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants a center tower flanked by two shorter outer sections.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for a plain block when the visible side wings frame the taller middle tower.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot uniquely shows a taller middle block with matching side wings and three windows.
